title: UK GDP quarterly national accounts, Apr-Jun 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the revision the Budget's forecast probably closes eight days too early to see
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/gdpquarterlynationalaccountsukapriltojune2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — reads verbatim 'GDP quarterly national accounts, UK: April to June 2026', '30 September 2026 at 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published', 'Revised quarterly estimate of gross domestic product (GDP) for the UK. Uses additional data to provide a more precise indication of economic growth than the first estimate', and carries the UK Statistics Authority accredited-official-statistics kitemark. Cadence corroborated from the publisher's own past-release listing (ons.gov.uk/economy/grossdomesticproductgdp/bulletins/quarterlynationalaccounts/previousreleases, fetched direct HTTP 200): the Q2 edition lands on the last day of September every year in the listing — 30 September 2025, 30 September 2024, 30 September 2023 — with the other three quarters on 30/31 June, 22/23 December and 28/31 March. Filed estimate on the same two counts as every ONS entry on this calendar: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a foreign national statistics institute, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Discovered 2026-09-09 during the never-assessed initial research of uk-public-sector-finances-2026-09-22
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-public-sector-finances-2026-09-22 LANE, 2026-09-09, because it is the exact 2026 analogue of a document the OBR is on the record as having EXCLUDED in 2024, and it is therefore the cleanest available test of when the 2026-10-28 Budget's forecast actually closes. In the 2024 round the OBR finalised its pre-measures forecast on 2024-09-26 and that forecast did NOT include the quarterly national accounts released 2024-09-30, which carried the Blue Book 2024 consistent revisions (search-relayed from the OBR's own published material; obr.uk returned 403 to this lane, recorded). Project the same convention forward — 34 to 36 days before 2026-10-28 is 2026-09-22 to 2026-09-24 — and the 2026-09-30 quarterly national accounts fall six to eight days outside it, so the EFO published with the Budget would be built on the first estimate rather than this revision. That makes this release informative in BOTH directions and it is registered as a forward test on the proposing lane's ledger (FT-uk-public-sector-finances-2026-09-22-4): if the 2026-10-28 EFO does incorporate it, the forecast closed later than either precedent and the sibling uk-public-sector-finances-2026-10-21 lane's central correction weakens; if it does not, the close is before 2026-09-30 and the 09-22 borrowing print is the boundary case its own ledger says it is. Tiered LOW and symbols [] on the same measured basis as the proposing lane: this repo tracks no UK-listed name and no house playbook is fiscal-, rates- or sterling-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this. The proposing lane makes no claim about this release's own market impact — it has not been measured, and the LOW tier is inherited from the family rather than argued from its own event study.
